title: Dictionary
bridge: `var price = new Dictionary<string, int>();` then `price["maize"] = 55;`, `price.TryGetValue(key, out int p)`, `price.ContainsKey(...)`, `price.GetValueOrDefault(key)`. Loop: `foreach (var (k, v) in price)` or `foreach (var kv in price)` with `kv.Key`, `kv.Value`.

exercises.title: Word counts
exercises.prompt: Write Count(string text) in class Words returning a SortedDictionary<string, int> of word counts (lowercase, any spaces).

tests.call: string.Join(" ", Words.Count("the cat and the hat"))

exercises.title: Inventory counts
exercises.prompt: A game inventory: write Add(Dictionary<string, int> bag, string item, int n) that adds n of an item (creating it if new) and Take(bag, item, n) that removes up to n and deletes the entry when it reaches 0. Take returns how many were actually taken.

tests.call: ((Func<string>)(() => { var b = new Dictionary<string, int>(); Bag.Add(b, "arrow", 10); Bag.Add(b, "arrow", 5); return b["arrow"].ToString(); }))()
((Func<string>)(() => { var b = new Dictionary<string, int>(); Bag.Add(b, "potion", 2); int t = Bag.Take(b, "potion", 5); return t + " " + b.ContainsKey("potion"); }))()

hints: Take: int have = bag.GetValueOrDefault(item); int t = Math.Min(have, n); then update or Remove.

explain: Explain dictionary to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
